events.asset: midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for post-traumatic stress disorder
events.title: FDA approval of midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for PTSD
events.proposition: The FDA approves midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for post-traumatic stress disorder.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date the FDA approval letter or Drugs@FDA entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) for midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) for post-traumatic stress disorder is dated, on any review cycle and under any sponsor name. A complete response letter, a positive advisory vote, a filing acceptance, a breakthrough designation or an expanded-access program is not an approval. A label narrower than PTSD (for example a PTSD subgroup or severity band) counts if the claim's indication reasonably includes it and the reading is logged at intake; a label that requires a REMS or a psychological-intervention component counts. Resolution source: Drugs@FDA, with the sponsor's press release as a secondary source. FALSE at the deadline when no such approval appears in Drugs@FDA.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA; sponsor press release as a secondary source

readings: Approval under any sponsor name (Lykos Therapeutics, MAPS PBC or a successor) counts; the entry is on the asset.
Eventual approval on any review cycle counts; the first-cycle proposal for the Lykos NDA under review in June 2024 (owen-1072, owen-1090, owen-1137, doblin-0031) is merged into this event.

'As it stands' (owen-1072) and 'at this stage' (owen-1090) refer to the NDA review cycle pending on the statement date; in the merged event a complete response letter is not an approval and does not by itself resolve the event.
MDMA-assisted therapy, MDMA-AT and midomafetamine name the same asset.
'MDMA' and 'get over the line' = FDA approval of the midomafetamine (MDMA-assisted therapy) NDA for PTSD that the post discusses; approval of MDMA for any other indication does not count.
A label with a REMS or a mandated psychological-intervention component counts as approval.

events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the sponsor's topline release, the ClinicalTrials.gov results posting or the peer-reviewed publication that first reports that MAPP1 (NCT03537014), the first Phase 3 trial of MDMA-assisted therapy for PTSD, met its prespecified primary endpoint (change in CAPS-5 total severity score versus placebo with therapy) with statistical significance as reported by the sponsor. events.asset: psilocybin (any psilocybin drug product, any sponsor, any indication)
events.title: FDA approval of a psilocybin drug product
events.proposition: The FDA approves a drug product whose active ingredient is psilocybin for any indication.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first FDA approval letter or Drugs@FDA entry (or the sponsor's approval announcement) for a drug product whose active ingredient is psilocybin, for any indication and under any sponsor (COMP360 by Compass Pathways, or another psilocybin product). readings: The forecaster names no indication or sponsor, so any psilocybin product for any indication counts.
'behind us' reads as reaching FDA approval after MDMA-assisted therapy; the event resolves on the FDA approval of psilocybin alone, without reference to the MDMA approval date.

'These substances' (MDMA and psilocybin, with 'psilocybin soon to follow' in the same passage) names the substance, not a sponsor or indication, so any psilocybin NDA approval for a psychiatric indication counts.
The event is on products whose active ingredient is psilocybin (as COMP360 is), not on analogues or other tryptamines.

events.asset: Cerebral prescribing and business practices (government enforcement action)
events.entity: US federal or state court, or federal or state enforcement agency (DOJ, DEA, FTC, state attorney general)
events.title: Cerebral: government enforcement outcome over its prescribing practices
events.proposition: A court or government agency convicts, sanctions, rules against, or accepts a settlement from Cerebral (or its executives) for regulatory violations or crimes in its prescribing or business practices.
events.criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a verdict, sentence, judgment, consent order or filed settlement in which a US federal or state court, or a federal or state enforcement agency (for example the Department of Justice, the DEA, the FTC, a state attorney general or a state medical board), convicts, sanctions, enters judgment against, or accepts a settlement or consent order from Cerebral, Inc. or a current or former Cerebral executive over Cerebral's controlled-substance prescribing or business practices. A subpoena, an announced investigation, an unresolved complaint or indictment, a private lawsuit or a voluntary policy change by Cerebral does not count. Resolution source: the court docket on CourtListener or PACER, with the DOJ or agency press release fixing the date of an agency settlement or order. FALSE at the deadline when no such docket entry or agency order exists.

resolution_source.name: Court docket (CourtListener or PACER); DOJ or agency press release as a secondary source

events.asset: SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy, accelerated iTBS) or another accelerated iTBS protocol for depression
events.entity: Magnus Medical, Stanford University, or another sponsor of an accelerated iTBS trial
events.title: SNT or accelerated iTBS for depression: a subsequent RCT meets its primary endpoint
events.proposition: A randomized controlled trial of SNT or another accelerated iTBS protocol for depression, reported after 11 July 2022, meets its prespecified primary endpoint with statistical significance.
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first sponsor topline release, ClinicalTrials.gov results posting or peer-reviewed publication dated after 2022-07-11 that reports a randomized controlled trial of SNT (Stanford Neuromodulation Therapy, the accelerated intermittent theta-burst TMS protocol commercialized by Magnus Medical) or another accelerated iTBS protocol for a depressive disorder, distinct from the Stanford SNT trial already published at the statement date, in which the prespecified primary efficacy endpoint met statistical significance versus the control arm as reported by the sponsor or the authors. Open-label series, secondary endpoints and pooled analyses do not count. Resolution source: the trial's ClinicalTrials.gov record and results posting, with the first peer-reviewed publication or sponsor release fixing the date. FALSE at the deadline when no such trial result has been reported.

resolution_source.name: ClinicalTrials.gov record and results posting of the trial; peer-reviewed publication or sponsor release as the secondary source
